chunks: Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Shah, the jurist of Marv, narrated in his house in Marv; Abu al-Qasim Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn al-Amir al-Ta'i at Basra narrated to me; my father narrated to me; Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him) narrated to me; my father Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) narrated to me; my father Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) narrated to me; my father Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon him) said; my father Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) narrated to me; my father Ali (peace be upon him) narrated to me; my father Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:
God the Mighty, the Exalted says: 'There is no god but God is My Stronghold. Whoever enters it is secure from My punishment.'

key_terms.لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: There is no god but God (Declaration of Monotheism)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of 'La ilaha illallah' as a fortress in Shia theology?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, this hadith qudsi traces its chain back through the Imams to the Prophet and God, emphasizing the theological weight of Tawhid as a divine sanctuary. It underscores the Shia belief that sincere affirmation of monotheism provides spiritual protection and security from divine retribution, linking the declaration directly to the concept of divine refuge.
